source_anchor: LeetCode #1 Two Sum (canonical formulation); CLRS §11.2 hashmap O(n) lookup pattern
prompt_text: Two-sum: find the pair of indices (i, j) with i<j such that nums[i] + nums[j] = target. For nums=[2, 7, 11, 15], target=9, print the index pair as JSON. Expected output: "[0,1]".

exec_cell.code: function ts(n,t){const m=new Map(); for(let i=0;i<n.length;i++){const c=t-n[i]; if(m.has(c))return [m.get(c),i]; m.set(n[i],i);} return null;} console.log(JSON.stringify(ts([2,7,11,15],9)));

candidate_responses.text: CORRECT: brute-force double loop returning [i,j] with i<j — slower but equivalent on this input.
WRONG: hashmap pattern correct but returns [i, m.get(c)] — swaps the order so the earlier index appears second.
candidate_responses.code: function ts(n,t){const m=new Map(); for(let i=0;i<n.length;i++){const c=t-n[i]; if(m.has(c))return [i,m.get(c)]; m.set(n[i],i);} return null;} console.log(JSON.stringify(ts([2,7,11,15],9)));

candidate_responses.text: CARGO-CULT: target / complement / includes vocabulary, but returns the matching VALUES [nums[i], complement] instead of the index pair.
candidate_responses.code: function twoSumPair(nums,target){for(let i=0;i<nums.length;i++){const complement=target-nums[i]; if(nums.includes(complement))return [nums[i],complement];} return null;} console.log(JSON.stringify(twoSumPair([2,7,11,15],9)));
